drills.q: True or false: a test suite passing against LocalStack is sufficient proof the same code will work against real AWS IAM policies.
drills.a: False -- AWS documentation states IAM policy evaluation and quotas are not fully modeled by emulators; a real staging AWS account is still needed for IAM/quota-sensitive validation.

drills.q: What sidecar container does Testcontainers use for automatic resource cleanup, and what triggers it?
drills.a: Ryuk -- it watches for the test-runner process's exit and removes every Testcontainers-labeled container/volume/network once the parent process dies.

drills.q: At single-user scale, are Ollama and vLLM's tokens/second roughly comparable or is there already a large gap?
drills.a: Roughly comparable -- both land in about the 130-180 tok/s band on the same hardware/model. The large gap (vLLM ~793 vs Ollama ~41 tok/s in one benchmark) appears specifically under concurrent load.

drills.q: A CI runner using Docker-in-Docker slowly runs out of disk space over several weeks with no single failing job pointing at the cause. What's the likely mechanism, and what's the fix?
drills.a: Ryuk's automatic cleanup is documented to fail on Docker-in-Docker/rootless-Docker CI, leaking Testcontainers-created containers silently. Fix: set TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true for that runner and add an explicit `docker container prune --filter "label=org.testcontainers=true"` step.

drills.q: Two engineers report different bugs from the same codebase despite both claiming to use 'the same devcontainer.' What's the likely misconfiguration?
drills.a: The devcontainer's base image is referenced by a mutable tag rather than a pinned digest -- the upstream image was rebuilt with different system package versions between when each engineer last built their container, so their actual environments silently diverged.

drills.q: Explain the architectural (not tuning-related) reason vLLM outperforms Ollama under concurrent load.
drills.a: vLLM implements continuous batching and PagedAttention-based KV-cache management specifically to serve many concurrent requests efficiently against shared GPU memory. Ollama, built on llama.cpp, is architected for single-user local convenience and doesn't implement the same concurrent-request-batching sophistication -- it's a structural design difference.

drills.q: Design a test suite for a service with a Postgres database and an S3 dependency. Assign each to LocalStack or Testcontainers and justify.
drills.a: Postgres -> Testcontainers: SQL dialect and constraint-enforcement fidelity matter for catching real bugs, worth the container startup cost. S3 (if the test is just 'did we call put_object correctly') -> LocalStack is sufficient and faster, since no IAM/quota-sensitive behavior is being exercised.

drills.q: A team's free-tier LocalStack dev environment resets all fixture data on every container restart, slowing onboarding. What are the two realistic options, and what does each cost?
drills.a: Script fast automatic fixture re-seeding at container startup (one-time engineering cost, also makes starting state version-controlled and explicit), or adopt LocalStack Cloud Pods (Base plan+, ~$45/month) for persistent state snapshot/restore across restarts -- an ongoing subscription cost.

drills.q: A team validated a RAG prototype entirely against Ollama locally, reports it's 'fast, ready to ship,' and wants to skip a load test before launch. What's the risk, and under what condition would skipping be reasonable?
drills.a: Risk: Ollama's single-user throughput says nothing about concurrent-load behavior, and the gap versus a production serving stack (e.g. vLLM) is architectural, not a missing tuning flag -- one benchmark shows a ~19x throughput gap under peak concurrent load. Skipping a dedicated load test is more reasonable only if genuine expected production concurrency stays in the single-digit range Ollama's benchmarks reasonably cover, and even then a lightweight concurrent smoke test is safer than none.

drills.q: Why is filtering `docker container prune` by the Testcontainers label important rather than pruning all stopped containers on a CI runner?
drills.a: A blanket prune could remove containers belonging to another concurrent job or process on the same shared runner that still needs them; filtering by the org.testcontainers=true label scopes cleanup to exactly the resources Ryuk would have been responsible for.

drills.q: What structural change happened to LocalStack's community and pro Docker image distribution in the 2026.3.0 release, and what does it NOT mean for free-tier users?
drills.a: The two images were unified into one; service access is now gated by auth-token entitlement instead of image choice. It does NOT mean the free tier gained access to everything pro has -- the free/Hobby tier still has a limited service subset and resets state on container restart; persistent state and broader coverage remain paid features.
